11 questions not to ask the tarot cards

1 October 2026

A bad question is the main reason people end up disappointed in tarot. The cards do not refuse to answer: they answer exactly what you asked. Let us go through the usual misses and what to ask instead.

1. “What awaits me?”

Too vague: the cards will show either the distant past or the distant future.

Instead: “Which events will matter for me in the next three months?”

2. “Will I get married this year?”

A yes/no question — the cards answer in images, not in a tick box.

Instead: “What do I need to understand about my relationship right now?”

3. “What does he think of me?”

That is access to someone else's head, which the cards do not have. What you get back is your own projection.

Instead: “What is going on between us, and what can I do?”

4. “When will he come back?”

Exact dates are not tarot's business, and tying yourself to someone else's decision turns you into a spectator.

Instead: “What can I lean on while the situation is still unclear?”

5. “How do I make him fall in love with me?”

That overrides another person's will. Such questions are both unethical and give a distorted answer.

Instead: “What in my behaviour is getting in the way of closeness?”

6. “How much will I earn?”

The cards do not hand out numbers.

Instead: “Which strategy will lead me to a stable income?”

7. “Will I be fired?”

The victim's seat.

Instead: “How can I show my value at work so that I am appreciated?”

8. “When will I die?” and any health question phrased as a diagnosis

Tarot does not replace a doctor. This is not superstition, just basic responsibility.

Instead: “What should I pay attention to in my condition?” — and then go to a specialist.

9. “Am I right?”

The cards do not confirm that you are right — they show the picture.

Instead: “What am I not seeing in this situation?”

10. “Why is everything bad for me?”

A question with no exit: it looks for someone to blame, not for a solution.

Instead: “What is stopping me from moving, and what first step is possible?”

11. The same question for the tenth time

Asking again until you like the answer is the most common way to spoil a reading. The second answer is not “more accurate” than the first, it is simply different.

A check before you lay the cards

Ask yourself three questions:

  • Is the question open — what, how, why?
  • Is it about me and my actions, not about other people's decisions?
  • Am I ready to hear any answer, not just the convenient one?

Three yeses — and the cards will speak to the point.

Phrased your question? Do a <a href="/taro/en/three-cards.html">three-card spread</a> or the <a href="/taro/en/celtic-cross.html">Celtic Cross</a> for a complicated situation.
